venue.name: Metchosin Pioneer Museum
venue.description: The Metchosin Pioneer Museum is a small volunteer run museum in a converted barn on Happy Valley Road, looked after by the Metchosin Museum Society. Inside are the Rocky Point stagecoach, recreated pioneer rooms, early photographs, and farm and logging implements, along with the Old Barn Books shop in the same building. Admission is free and it opens to the public on Sunday mornings. Museum curators also run booked school field trips and small group tours by appointment.

facility_notes.washrooms: The groups may have a snack and/or lunch, washroom break, and then visit the other museum.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The groups may have a snack and/or lunch, washroom break, and then visit the other museum.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Schoolhouse Museum is fully wheelchair accessible. The Pioneer Museum is partially accessible.

venue.hours_notes: Open to the public on Sundays from 11:00 to 14:00. Closed on statutory holidays.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Pioneer Museum is open year round on Sundays. School field trips run September to June.

programs.name: School Field Trip
programs.description: Museum curators take a booked class through both of the Society's museums on the same visit. Half the class tours the Pioneer Museum and sees the Rocky Point stagecoach, artifacts from a pioneer kitchen, home and parlour, early photographs, and farm and logging implements. The other half spends that time at the Schoolhouse Museum across the road, then the two halves swap over with a break for a snack or lunch and washrooms in between. The site gives the length as 30, 45 or 60 minutes for each museum depending on the grade, and the cost as five dollars per student. It runs September to June on Thursdays and Fridays, and you book it through a form on their site.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through a converted barn looking at the stagecoach, the pioneer kitchen and parlour, old photographs and the farm and logging tools while a curator explains what each one was for. In the Schoolhouse half of the visit they sit at old desks, write with a dip pen and ink, spin a button on a string and hunt for artifacts.
programs.our_note: The whole visit is built around splitting a class in two, so bring enough adults to keep both halves moving. The Pioneer Museum is only partly accessible, so say up front if anyone in your group uses a wheelchair or a walker. Ask whether the five dollars covers both museums or only one, because the page does not say.
programs.practical_summary: There are washrooms and the visit is built around a snack or lunch break, though the site does not say where you eat. The Pioneer Museum is only partly accessible, and bus parking, a wet weather plan and how many adults you need are all unstated, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: Cost: F i v e  d o l l a r s/student

programs.name: Small Group Tour by Appointment
programs.description: Museum curators also show small groups round the Pioneer Museum by appointment, outside the Sunday opening hours. The tour covers the Rocky Point stagecoach, artifacts from a pioneer kitchen, bedroom and parlour, early photographs, and farm and logging implements. It can be paired with the Society's Schoolhouse Museum on the same day, or booked separately, in which case the site says there is a cost for the second day. The price itself is not published. You ask about dates through a form on their site.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the converted barn with a curator, looking at the stagecoach, the recreated pioneer rooms, old photographs and the farm and logging tools, and hearing what each one was used for.
programs.our_note: This is the way in if a Sunday morning does not suit you or your group is too small for the school field trip. No price is published anywhere, so ask for it in the same message you use to ask about dates. Doing the two museums on separate days costs extra, so try to fit both into one visit.
programs.practical_summary: Booking goes through a form on their site and no phone number or email is published, so allow time for a reply. The price, the group size they can take and whether you can eat on site are all unstated for this tour.
programs.extra_fees_note: If the two museums are booked on separate days, the site says there will be a cost for the second day.
programs.evidence: Museum curators offer tours in both the Schoolhouse and Pioneer Museums to small groups by appointment.

images.alt: Two children write with pens at a wooden desk beside an upright piano, in a room with framed documents and old photographs on the walls.

gaps: This record covers the Pioneer Museum only. The Metchosin Museum Society runs it together with the Schoolhouse Museum across the road at 4475 Happy Valley Road, and the field trip is written up as a single visit that splits a class between the two buildings, so the price, the timings, the accessibility note and the booking form are shared between them.

The price is written on their page with spaces between the letters, as 'F i v e  d o l l a r s/student'. It is five dollars per student, and the page does not say whether that covers one museum or both.

No age or grade range is published. The booking form asks for a grade level and a number of students, so it is set up for school classes, but nothing says whether preschool or daycare groups are taken or how young a child can be.

No minimum or maximum group size is published for the Pioneer Museum. The small group tour page gives a maximum occupancy of 12 visitors, but that figure is written against the Schoolhouse Museum, not this one, so it has not been recorded here.
How long a visit lasts is given as 30, 45 or 60 minutes for each museum depending on the grade, so there is no single figure to record.
How much notice they need to book, how many adults have to come, and whether accompanying adults pay are not stated anywhere.
Where a group eats is not stated. The page says groups may have a snack or lunch and a washroom break between the two museums, but not whether that space is indoors or outdoors.
Bus parking and a wet weather plan are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
There is no phone number or email address published. The only way to reach the Society is the forms on their booking, tours and contact pages, each of which uses a CAPTCHA.
The price for the small group tour by appointment is not published. The page only says that booking the two museums on separate days costs extra.
months unknown for the small group tour by appointment. Only the school field trip states a season.

The two photographs on the field trip page both show the Schoolhouse side of the visit rather than the Pioneer Museum, so only one of them has been recorded here and its alt text describes just what is in the frame.

Much of the background writing on the Pioneer Museum page was prepared in November 2018, but the field trip page itself was updated in April 2026, so the price and the days offered are current rather than stale.
Alt text for the photograph of two children writing was written after opening the image in a browser and looking at it. The other three use the words the site itself supplies, which are brief.
